audiences.executive: Desktops and applications people can use from anywhere, quickly, without the data leaving the data centre.
audiences.technical: Images, profiles and pools managed centrally, with logon time watched and capacity that grows for peaks.
audiences.financial: Fewer laptops to secure and refresh; capacity for the peak paid for only when the peak comes.

objections.says: Users hate virtual desktops: they are slow.
objections.clarify: Which users and applications, and what was measured?
objections.answer: Measure logon and application times for real users, and agree the target before the test.
objections.prove: Measure the logon time of a group of real users against the agreed target.

objections.says: Our designers and engineers cannot work on virtual desktops.
objections.clarify: Which applications, and how many users?
objections.answer: Give them GPU-backed desktops sized for their applications, and test with their own work.
objections.prove: A designer does a real task on a GPU-backed desktop and signs off the experience.

objections.says: Desktops in one data centre are a single point of failure.
objections.clarify: What happens to users today if the site is down?
objections.answer: Plan a second site or cloud capacity for desktops, with profiles replicated.
objections.prove: Fail a test pool over and have users log on at the other site.
